card.name: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll
card.tagline: A high-speed, athletic partner dance blending rock music with gymnastic acrobatics.
card.profile: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll is a competitive dance sport derived from Lindy Hop and Boogie Woogie, characterized by rapid kick-step footwork and complex gymnastic maneuvers. It is performed in pairs or groups, with routines strictly regulated by the World Rock'N'Roll Confederation (WRRC) to ensure safety during high-speed lifts and flips. The dance is performed to fast-paced pop or disco music, emphasizing precision and athletic endurance.
card.insight: Dancers perform at such high intensity that a 90-second routine is physically equivalent to running an 800-meter race.

card.profile_long: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll is a highly technical, athletic dance form that evolved from the mid-20th-century swing tradition. Emerging from the Lindy Hop and later the Boogie Woogie, the dance was transformed into a choreographed sport in the 1970s, particularly in France and across Europe. Unlike social rock dancing, this form is designed for competition and performance, requiring immense physical conditioning. The dance is structured around a 4/4 meter, with a focus on a rapid, repetitive kick-step footwork pattern. Dancers perform on the balls of their feet to maintain the speed required for the 176-208 bpm tempo. The choreography is divided into two distinct components: footwork sequences and acrobatic elements. The latter includes lifts, throws, jumps, and flips, which are strictly categorized by the World Rock'N'Roll Confederation (WRRC) based on the age and skill level of the dancers. Safety is a primary concern, leading to the development of specialized elastic costumes that allow for freedom of movement and durability during complex maneuvers. The dance is typically performed by young athletes, as the physical demand of the sport is significant. Competitions are judged on three main criteria: foot technique, overall artistic impression, and the quality of the acrobatic elements. The sport continues to evolve, with national and international federations standardizing rules to balance the spectacle of the acrobatics with the safety of the participants.

sections.origins_and_history: The dance originated from the Lindy Hop, which appeared around 1920, and evolved through the Boogie Woogie of the 1940s. By 1955, as rock music gained popularity, the dance form began to shift toward a more competitive, acrobatic style. In the 1970s, French dance schools in Lyon helped formalize the discipline, leading to the creation of the World Rock'N'Roll Confederation (WRRC).
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance relies on a 6-basic or 9-basic step structure. The 9-basic step is the modern tournament standard, characterized by a 'kick-ball-change' maneuver. Dancers move in a linear fashion, maintaining a precise, upright posture while executing kicks into the air. Acrobatics are integrated into the routine, ranging from simple lifts to complex flips, depending on the competition class.
sections.music_and_instruments: The dance is performed to 4/4 time music, typically modern disco or pop tracks played at high speeds between 176 and 208 bpm. The rhythm emphasizes the first and third beats of each measure, differing from the off-beat stress found in traditional rock music.
sections.costume_and_setting: Dancers wear custom-made, multicoloured costumes crafted from elastic, durable artificial fibers. These are designed to be tight-fitting to prevent snagging during acrobatics. Footwear consists of light jazz shoes for dance programs or aerobics sneakers for acrobatic programs to provide grip and shock absorption.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll is primarily a competitive sport. It is performed at local, national, and international championships organized by the WRRC. The focus is on precision, athleticism, and the successful execution of high-difficulty acrobatic elements.
sections.notable_figures: Notable figures include French world champion Miguel Angueira and Katerina Tikhonova, who has competed in the sport.
sections.regional_variants: Categories are divided by age and skill level, including Youth, Juniors, and Main Class (Contact Style and Free Style). Rules regarding allowed acrobatics vary by these categories to ensure safety.
sections.lineage: Swing (1920s) -> Lindy Hop -> Boogie Woogie (1940s) -> Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll (1955-present).

teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with the 6-basic step in dance schools before progressing to the 9-basic tournament step.

claims.text: Acrobatic Rock'n'Roll originated from Lindy Hop and evolved into a choreographed sport.
The dance is performed to 4/4 music at 176-208 bpm.
The modern tournament standard uses a 9-basic step.
Costumes are made of elastic artificial fiber for safety and freedom of movement.
The sport is recognized by the International Olympic Committee.
A 90-second routine is physically equivalent to an 800-meter race.
